ground_truth_core_content:
Introduction:
**1:** The generated section covers the closed-book exam framing, fine-tuning limitations (resource-heavy, dataset curation, catastrophic forgetting, plus an added pre-training-cost detail), and context-window/lost-in-the-middle limitations (with a 500-page-report/financial-figure example) with the same substance as the expected section. The brief "advanced, agentic patterns" preview mirrors the expected section's own preview at a reduced level of detail; per the standing ruling this is not penalized since the essential idea is still present. The Lesson-10 memory contrast and RAG-as-open-book-exam solution are both present and substantively equivalent.

The RAG System: Core Components:
**1:** Both sections cover the same three pillars — Retrieval, Augmentation, and Generation — with matching substance and no notable omissions.

The RAG Pipeline: Ingestion and Retrieval:
**0:** Both sections cover the same two-phase structure with matching substance, and both reference Lesson 4's structured outputs. The generated section notably includes filtering capabilities in the Search step ("Advanced systems can also leverage filtering capabilities within the vector database...") — an addition relative to the expected section, which does not mention this either, so it does not affect this score either way. However, as in every replicate of this lesson graded so far, two ideas present in the expected section remain absent: (1) the callout on long-context/asymmetric-search embedding models; (2) the guidance on tuning chunk size empirically against retrieval metrics (hit rate/recall, MRR@k, nDCG@k) and the specific chunk-size/overlap ranges.

Advanced RAG Techniques:
**1:** Both sections cover the same six techniques — Hybrid Search, Re-ranking, Query Transformations, Advanced Chunking, GraphRAG, and Metadata Filtering — with matching substance. The generated section's numerous added statistics and technical details (knowledge drift/retrieval decay, the Cornell/NVIDIA latency finding, the multiphase re-ranking architecture, ontology-guided GraphRAG construction, domain-specific regulatory considerations, and Self-Query Retrieval) are additions rather than omissions and don't affect the core ideas, which are otherwise complete.

Agentic RAG:
**1:** Both sections cover the standard-vs-agentic distinction, the ReAct-loop tie-in, and all four agentic capabilities — iterative refinement, source selection, information fusion, and the knowledge-base-update capability correctly previewed as an open memory-management question — plus the same Thought/Action/Observation worked example.

Conclusion:
**1:** Both sections cover the same key takeaways: RAG as the primary industry solution to the LLM knowledge problem, the necessity of advanced techniques for production quality, the agentic future of retrieval, the three core benefits, RAG's status as a foundational competency and subset of Context Engineering, and the same transition preview into Lesson 10 plus future topics.
